To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

anomalous J / psi suppression at RHIC (and SPS) can be described by a hadronic baseline, and that the puzzling rapidity dependece of the PHENICX data is reproduced as an effect of the longer path for J / psi production at forward rapidities.
the anomalous J / Ψ suppression at RHIC can be explained by absorption in a hot hadron gas, which successfully describes statistical particle production, without invoking any additional mechanism.
the observed anomalous suppression of J/ψ mesons at RHIC and at SPS can be understood as the result of absorption by a hadron resonance background.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the production of heavy quarks and their bound states in high energy nuclear collisions, in particular in the context of the heavy-ion program of the Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collider (RHIC) at Brookhaven National Laboratory.
the study of the properties of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) formed in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
the study of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) produced at RHIC and LHC energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the J / ψ suppression observed in heavy ion collisions at RHIC is due to a combination of the effects of a dense hadron gas and a deconfined quark–gluon plasma.
the observed suppression of J / ψ is due to the absorption by a hadron resonance medium.
the J / ψ suppression is a consequence of the hot and dense hadronic phase which is produced in the heavy ion collision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the J / ψ suppression is a hadron gas effect, and the observed suppression at RHIC is not due to a deconfined phase of matter, but to a hadronic gas.
the observed anomalous suppression is consistent with hadronic final state interactions and can be explained without invoking a new phase of QCD matter.
the anomalous suppression of J / ψ is not necessarily a signal of the quark–gluon plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the J / ψ is not a good thermometer for the quark gluon plasma.
a hadronic baseline for J / ψ suppression is a viable explanation for the observed data.
a hadron gas baseline is sufficient to describe the J / ψ data at SPS and RHIC, without the need to invoke a quark-gluon plasma phase.
